title: Ops-led inference econ kickoff - Horizon Capital
summary: Intro discovery between Redwood AE/SE and Horizon Cap ops/product/security. Primary focus: per-token economics, latency budget for LLM features, tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem), and what a pilot looks like. Customer has strict data residency and mid-six-figure annual budget ceiling; wants unit-cost clarity and a short benchmark pilot before procurement.
next_steps: Maya to send detailed per-token pricing and example unit-econ spreadsheet by 2027-08-13
Liam to propose benchmark config + test harness and sample prompt set by 2027-08-16
Horizon to share expected QPS pattern and three canonical prompts by 2027-08-14
Schedule 60m technical pilot kickoff for week of 2027-08-23
action_items: Maya Chen - send pricing + pilot proposal - 2027-08-13
Liam Ortiz - bench harness config and cost model spreadsheet - 2027-08-16
Arjun Patel - share workload profile and SLAs (P95 target) - 2027-08-14
Kelly Zhang - list of compliance docs required (SOC2 report, IP allowlist, KMS patterns) - 2027-08-18
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Arjun Patel (Horizon - Head of MLOps), Sophie Grant (VP Product), Marco Ruiz (Infra), Kelly Zhang (Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. We're Redwood, I'm Maya, I'm the AE working with Horizon. With me is Liam, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Arjun Patel: Doing good, thanks. We're excited to kick this off. We've been evaluating a few directions and wanted to dig into the economics and the deploy options.
[00:13] Sophie Grant: Hi all, yes, from a product perspective we need to understand per-call cost and latency targets before we scope rollout.
[00:19] Liam Ortiz: Great. Quick agenda from our side: confirm your workload (QPS, seq lengths), discuss per-token pricing and the levers (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization), map Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for your constraints, then agree next steps for a short benchmark/pilot. Sound OK?
[00:32] Marco Ruiz: Yep, that's what we need. Also we have some strict residency and encryption requirements which may push us toward VPC or private.
[00:39] Kelly Zhang: Right, we'll need SOC 2, audit logs, KMS integration, SSO. But cost is a blocker too — we have a mid-six-figure yearly budget target for inference.

[02:12] Liam Ortiz: Cool, Arjun, can you walk us through the workloads you expect? Peak QPS, average tokens per request, typical prompt sizes?
[02:20] Arjun Patel: Sure. We're building an assistant inside our analytics dashboard. Typical requests are 150-250 tokens prompt, 30-80 tokens generation. Avg QPS now is low, like 2-3 RPS, but peak can hit 25-30 during reports. We expect growth to maybe 100 RPS in 12 months. We care about P95 latency around 300-400ms for most interactive flows, some async flows can be up to 2s.
[02:47] Liam Ortiz: Thanks. That makes a lot of sense. For that profile, per-token economics will be heavily influenced by sequence length, batching, and whether you're OK with slightly higher cold-start latencies. Also whether you want to pin models to dedicated GPUs.

[05:05] Maya Chen: Quick context on pricing: our Hosted API has straightforward per-token rates and we surface model-specific unit costs. Dedicated is subscription/reserved with committed throughput and lower per-token unit because you amortize GPU time. Private (VPC/on-prem) adds infra/ops cost and typically has a longer procurement cycle. We can run numbers side-by-side based on your 3-month, 12-month projected usage.
[05:34] Sophie Grant: So how big is the gap between Hosted and Dedicated? Ballpark per-token?
[05:39] Liam Ortiz: Ballpark depends on model choice and effective batching. For medium-sized open models you might see Hosted at X cents per 1k tokens, Dedicated can be 30-60% lower when fully utilized. But if utilization is low, Dedicated can be more expensive because of committed capacity. The real lever for you will be batching and prefix/KV cache on repeated queries. If you have lots of similar prompts, cache hits reduce tokens processed substantially.

[07:12] Marco Ruiz: Can you explain the prefix/KV cache — I'm not sure how much of our workload will hit it.
[07:18] Liam Ortiz: Sure. If users often ask variations of the same prompt or you have a canonical context (like account history) that gets attached, Redwood's KV cache stores recent key-value cache entries for the model's attention so later requests reuse previous activations, reducing recompute. It's most beneficial for sessions with repeat tokens like system prompts and long context tails. We also do continuous batching to fill GPU batches without raising P95 too much.

[09:01] Arjun Patel: That sounds promising. Our usage has a lot of repeated structure — similar system prompts and templated questions — so cache hit rate could be high. How do you throttle or control batching to meet our 300-400ms P95?
[09:15] Liam Ortiz: We provide configurable latency SLOs and batching window caps. For example, you can set a max batching delay of 10-20ms to keep latency low and still get batching benefits. There are also routing policies: route low-latency traffic to dedicated pools and background/async traffic to cheaper variants.

[11:30] Kelly Zhang: On security, we need to know what we get for Hosted — can data be or remain in customer-only storage? KMS? Auditability?
[11:39] Maya Chen: Hosted keeps user payloads encrypted in transit; we can integrate with your KMS for key wrap on Private deployments. For Hosted enterprise customers we offer configurable retention and audit logs, and we can provide SOC2 documentation. If you need full network isolation, that's where Dedicated VPC or Private on-prem comes in. We'll attach an RDOC packet with details.

[13:05] Sophie Grant: I want to make sure we're not underestimating cost for peak traffic. If we hit 100 RPS in 12 months, what does unit cost look like?
[13:13] Liam Ortiz: We'll run the numbers. Important inputs: average tokens/request, percent of served by cache, batching efficiency (effective tokens/GPU-step), and model quantization profile. We'll propose a few variants: Hosted with autoscale, Dedicated reserved pool sized for 99th percentile with burst, and Private with expected infra ops. We'll show per-1000-token costs, plus amortized infra ops for Private.

[16:00] Marco Ruiz: Speaking of quantization — do you support int8/4-bit that changes performance?
[16:06] Liam Ortiz: Yes, our inference runtime supports quantized kernels and we can recommend quantization per model. Quantization reduces memory footprint so more throughput per GPU and lower cost but sometimes small quality delta. We'll run evals to measure ROUGE/other metrics for your prompts.

[18:30] Arjun Patel: Procurement will need a rough TCO for a year. Can you give a scenario: 5k monthly active users, average 5 requests/day/user, average 200 tokens in, 50 out, ~cache-hit 20%?
[18:45] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll put together a TCO spreadsheet with scenarios. Quick rough calc: that's roughly 5k * 5 * (200+50) = 6.25M tokens/month before cache. With 20% cache + batching, effective billable tokens might be closer to 4M. We'll show Hosted vs Dedicated amortized numbers.

[21:02] Sophie Grant: What about fallbacks? If a dedicated pool is overloaded do you fail open to Hosted? We need reliability.
[21:09] Liam Ortiz: Standard patterns are canary and fallback routing. Redwood can route to a higher-cost hosted fallback or queue requests depending on policy. We can set per-route fallbacks for critical flows.

[23:20] Marco Ruiz: How invasive is Private? We can't be boxed into a long migration.
[23:26] Maya Chen: Private has the longest lead time because of infra provisioning and network setup, but we ship a customer-managed control plane that mirrors the hosted console. For many clients, they start with Hosted or Dedicated to validate unit economics and then transition to Private if required.

[26:10] Kelly Zhang: On compliance, can you support bring-your-own-key for Hosted or do we need Private?
[26:15] Liam Ortiz: For Hosted enterprise you can have envelope keys and HSM integrations for certain patterns; full BYOK where keys never leave your HSM generally maps to Private. We'll include the exact cryptography patterns in the security packet.

[29:40] Arjun Patel: Let's talk pilot: we want a short benchmark against our prompt set that measures latency P50/P95, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. What's the typical scope and timeline?
[29:50] Maya Chen: Typical pilot is 2-3 weeks. Stage 1: Redwood runs a controlled bench on Hosted/Dedicated configs with your sample prompts and traffic patterns. Stage 2: If you want, a short Dedicated trial with reserved capacity for a week to validate production behavior. We'll provide a bench harness and the per-token cost breakdown.

[32:12] Sophie Grant: Will Redwood run the bench or do we run it in our environment?
[32:18] Liam Ortiz: We can do either. Many customers ask us to run initial bench on Hosted for speed, then we hand over the harness you can run inside your VPC or Dedicated pool. We'll produce CSVs with per-token counts, latency percentiles, and cost model outputs.

[34:55] Marco Ruiz: Data residency — we need EU-only storage for logs, and retention rules. Can Hosted guarantee region residency?
[35:03] Maya Chen: Yes, we have EU regions and can restrict where data is stored. We can also sign a data processing addendum for EU requirements. For stricter controls you might prefer Dedicated in your cloud region or Private.

[37:40] Kelly Zhang: One more question: what about RBAC and tenant isolation? We'll have multiple internal teams using the same instance.
[37:46] Liam Ortiz: Redwood Console supports token- and route-level RBAC, audit logs, and per-route cost breakdowns. For Dedicated/Private you can also enforce VPC-level network segmentation.

[40:00] Maya Chen: Ok, before we wrap, recap and deliverables. We'll produce: pricing scenarios and a TCO spreadsheet, a benchmark harness + recommended config, and a security doc packet (SOC2, KMS patterns, network docs). Horizon to share prompt set and traffic profile. Proposed pilot kickoff week of 2027-08-23.

[40:18] Arjun Patel: Sounds good. Procurement will need a simple pilot statement of work and that TCO to show to finance.
[40:26] Maya Chen: We'll include a pilot SOW template.

[42:10] Sophie Grant: Any gotchas we should watch for?
[42:14] Liam Ortiz: Two things: 1) if you underutilize Dedicated the math can invert, so we recommend a careful utilization projection; 2) prefilling cache and shaping traffic improves effective cost dramatically, so instrumenting client-side caching and session affinity helps.

[44:00] Kelly Zhang: Ok, thanks — we'll assemble the data and pull in procurement.
[44:07] Maya Chen: Great. I'll send the pricing and proposal tomorrow-ish and Liam will share the bench config. Thanks everyone.
[44:17] Arjun Patel: Thanks all.

Meeting end
notes: Prospect is ops-led with clear budget ceiling and residency requirements. Strong signal to start with Hosted bench then evaluate Dedicated. Important to present clear utilization sensitivity analysis.
